title: Vectors: Dynamic Collections
learningObjectives: Append, access and update vector elements.
Use size and empty to guard operations.
Remove elements only when valid and understand invalidation.
Use range-based traversal for element processing.

understand.concept: std::vector is a dynamically sized sequence. push_back adds elements; size and empty describe the collection.
understand.whyItMatters: Vectors fit collections whose size changes at runtime.
understand.explain: Check bounds, emptiness, and iterator/reference invalidation after growth.

examples.title: Grow vector
examples.explanation: push_back appends and grows the collection.

examples.title: Empty test
examples.explanation: empty is true before any items are added.

examples.title: Remove final item
examples.explanation: pop_back removes the last item; call only when non-empty.

practise.guidedTask: For Vectors: Dynamic Collections, trace each example and record the collection type, size/capacity where relevant, valid index range, values before and after each operation, and what the code prints. Identify the key boundary case.
practise.independentTask: Write a C++ mini-task focused on Vectors: Dynamic Collections: use a small collection of values/text, perform at least three meaningful operations, and test normal, empty or boundary, and invalid-index/input cases. Explain your collection choice and expected output.
hints: Select the collection type and justify its size behavior.
Trace initialization and current element values.
Use bounds-aware access for potentially invalid indexes.
Prefer direct traversal when the index is not required.
Test empty, first, last and out-of-range scenarios.

questions.explanation: Removing from an empty vector is invalid.
